properties.areaDesc: Stephens
properties.headline: Wildfire with IMMEDIATE EVACUATION for Velma.
properties.description: At 2:10 PM  a large and destructive wildfire was burning out of control W of Velma spreading rapidly NE. Wildfires can damage or destroy structures and can harm or kill people and animals. For your safety EVACUATE IMMEDIATELY for The Stephens County Fairgrounds.
properties.instruction:
Those between Sanner Road and Hargrove Street should LEAVE this area NOW to avoid injury or death. Do not delay to pack belongings. Reunification Center is setting up at Stephens County Fairgrounds.
Roads in the area may be impacted by fire and smoke. Never drive into heavy smoke. SLOW DOWN & MOVE OVER for emergency vehicles.

CMAMtext: Stephens CO EM: EVACUATION ORDER for Location for a wildfire. LEAVE NOW to the Direction.
CMAMlongtext: Jurisdiction EM: A dangerous wildfire is located Location spreading rapidly Direction. This area is in IMMEDIATE DANGER from wildfires which can cause injury/death, burn down homes/other structures. LEAVE NOW toward the Evacuation Center. Do not delay to pack belongings. Never drive into heavy smoke.

properties.areaDesc: Pamlico Sound; S of Cape Hatteras NC to Ocracoke Inlet NC out to 20 NM
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 24 at 4:06PM EDT until August 24 at 4:30PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
For the following areas...
Pamlico Sound...
S of Cape Hatteras NC to Ocracoke Inlet NC out to 20 NM...

At 406 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing waterspouts
was located near The Center Of The Pamlico Sound, or 8 nm southwest
of Pamlico Sound, moving east at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

Locations impacted include...
Pamlico Sound, Hatteras Village, and The Center Of The Pamlico Sound.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Frequent lightning is occurring with this storm. If caught on the
open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...
Illinois...

Wabash River from Montezuma to Mount Carmel

White River from Elliston to Hazleton

.Minor flooding continues along portions of central Indiana rivers
due to excessive rain over the previous few weeks. Largely dry
weather is in store for the week ahead, with only a few low chances
of rain.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Mount Carmel.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, River is bankfull in all locations.  All
oil field production ceases with the exception of pumping units on
substructures.  Access to these are by boat only.  Agricultural
losses increase dramatically.  Farmers move livestock to higher
ground.  City of Mount Carmel leaves flood gates B and C in year
round.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:45 AM CDT /12:45 PM EDT/ Monday the stage was 19.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:45 AM CDT /12:45 PM EDT/ Monday was 19.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.1 feet
early Thursday morning. It will then fall below flood stage early
Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 130 AM CDT /230 AM
EDT/.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 24 at 1:34PM MDT until August 24 at 4:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Babylon burn scar in...
Central San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* Until 430 PM MDT.

* At 134 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Babylon Burn Scar over Dark Canyon. Between 0.5
and 0.8 inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1
to 3 inches in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation
and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Babylon Burn Scar over
Dark Canyon.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Babylon Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Dark Canyon
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Babylon Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
through slot canyons and steep terrain below Dark Canyon..climb to
safety.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Arroyos, streams, and rivers can become raging currents in a matter
of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:30 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:30 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 24 at 9:46AM CDT by NWS Lincoln IL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Illinois...

Illinois River at Beardstown affecting Brown, Cass, Morgan and
Schuyler Counties.

.The following forecasts are based on observed precipitation, soil
moisture conditions, and forecast precipitation.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Illinois River at Beardstown.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, Seepage problems begin in the Lost Creek
Drainage and Levee District.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM CDT Monday the stage was 16.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:45 AM CDT Monday was 16.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 14.0 feet Monday,
August 31.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Persons with interests along this river need to remain aware of the
latest forecasts and associated flood risk for their area. Stay tuned
for further updates on this flooding situation.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1230 AM CDT.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...
Illinois...

Wabash River at New Harmony affecting Wabash, Gibson, White, Posey
and Gallatin Counties.

For the Wabash River...including New Harmony...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at New Harmony.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning to Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, The river overflows low ground on the
Illinois side.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM CDT Monday the stage was 14.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
tomorrow morning to a crest of 15.6 feet early Thursday
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage early Saturday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.6
feet on 05/26/2020.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.
